translated_text: On the train to & earth 16. 4. 36 My dear little Zabalein. I'm standing on the train right now and it's shaking terribly. If this continues, I'll have to give up my good intention of writing to you live. I couldn't continue writing, so the letter will only be finished in Chomutov. Zabalein, the weather is so wonderfully beautiful; everyone is smiling at you, people are in a better mood, and Bob would love to get up to some mischief with exuberance. Business is going well too. It seems that we are slowly but surely making a name for ourselves. But with this beautiful weather, a longing always awakens in me again, which is then broken. – I miss you so much, and simple, friendly attempts to compensate for all the young people's disappointment are unsuccessful. Write to me, Zabal, when you're going on holiday this year. We really must see each other again soon! – Or will you like it so much in England in the end that you won't want to come back?!! You must also tell me in detail about your work there and your circle of acquaintances. Your toe I am - Joh I am almost a little Rifersnelitio. Egge came back from Aflum yesterday without being in Paris. Apart from the fact that I thought it was stupid of him, he couldn't achieve anything there. He had to come back and will probably - unless we have extraordinary luck - be drafted into the military on April 21st. We have already come to terms with it and are trying to adjust completely today. Of course, I am even more indispensable at home now. The girl has almost completely recovered in the meantime. She is 29 years old and won't laugh, she'll be getting married in 2-3 months. But you don't need to be afraid, not me, but a rich, young, and handsome director general. She still loves me very much, but after I told her that I couldn't advise her to marry me, that she was after all 29 years old and had to think about marriage, she agreed with me with two tearful eyes. I've already spoken with him and got the best impression of him – not your everyday life, but at least a happy ending. I think it's very nice to meet Trugard Hahn. I know her very well – yes, she was perhaps the Liesel Hite Jansen school to me. She's an extremely good friend, and I also think very highly of her abilities. She's destined for fashion, the most talented young girl I know. I hope she soon finds the right field of work so she can progress. I haven't received a letter from her. Do you know her address?! Little one, I long for her so much. Write to me soon, Zob.
